import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Filter to expression features
    expr_ids = [fid for fid, typ in zip(feats.ids, feats.types) if typ == 'expression']
    expr_cols = [feats.column(fid) for fid in expr_ids]
    
    # Check if any expression features exist
    if not expr_cols:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Get expression data
    X_expr = feats.x[:, expr_cols]
    
    # Standardize
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_expr)
    
    # Compute correlation matrix
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(X_scaled.T)
    
    # Find highly correlated pairs (|r| >= 0.6)
    high_corr_pairs = []
    for i in range(len(expr_ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(expr_ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i, j]) >= 0.6:
                high_corr_pairs.append((expr_ids[i], expr_ids[j]))
    
    # If we have correlated pairs, look for modules using PCA
    if high_corr_pairs:
        # Use PCA to find principal components
        pca = PCA(n_components=min(3, len(expr_ids)))
        pc_scores = pca.fit_transform(X_scaled)
        
        # Look for dominant PC that explains significant variance
        explained_variance_ratio = pca.explained_variance_ratio_
        
        # Select top PC with > 10% variance explained
        if len(explained_variance_ratio) > 0 and explained_variance_ratio[0] > 0.1:
            # Get loadings for first component
            loadings = dict(zip(expr_ids, pca.components_[0]))
            
            # Sort by absolute loading values to get most important features
            sorted_features = sorted(loadings.items(), key=lambda x: abs(x[1]), reverse=True)
            
            # Select top features (up to MAX_DRIVERS-1 since we might need one for driver)
            selected_features = [fid for fid, _ in sorted_features[:MAX_DRIVERS-1]]
            
            # Also include the feature with highest absolute loading as driver
            driver_feature = sorted_features[0][0]
            
            # Ensure driver is not already in selected features
            if driver_feature not in selected_features:
                selected_features = [driver_feature] + selected_features
                
            # Take at most MAX_DRIVERS
            drivers = tuple(selected_features[:MAX_DRIVERS])
            
            # Return design with all expression features as columns, 
            # and the weighted score from PCA
            return Design(
                drivers=drivers,
                columns=tuple(expr_ids),
                products=(),
                loadings=loadings
            )
    
    # If no strong correlations, use simple t-test approach
    t_stats = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(expr_ids):
        group0 = X_scaled[feats.y == 0, i]
        group1 = X_scaled[feats.y == 1, i]
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(group0, group1, equal_var=False)
        t_stats.append((abs(t_stat), fid))
    
    # Sort by t-statistic and select top features
    t_stats.sort(reverse=True)
    top_features = [fid for _, fid in t_stats[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
    
    # Return design with top features as drivers and columns
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(top_features),
        columns=tuple(expr_ids),
        products=(),
        loadings={}
    )
